title: Morocco's Bet on Africa: Phosphate, Banks, Ports and the Nigeria Gas Pipeline | The Six, Ep. 5
lede: Morocco holds about two-thirds of the world's phosphate rock reserves, and its banks now operate in 27 African countries. This episode looks at Morocco's business ties across the continent since it rejoined the African Union in 2017: phosphate, banking, ports, and a planned gas pipeline from Nigeria.
keyPoints: Morocco holds 50 billion tonnes of phosphate rock reserves, about 68% of the world's 73 billion, and mined an estimated 36 million tonnes in 2025, second only to China (USGS, 2026).

Moroccan banking groups operate in 27 African countries; 1,520 of their 1,659 branches abroad are in Africa. For the three pan-African groups, Africa outside Morocco was 22% of assets and 31% of net profit in 2025 (Bank Al-Maghrib, July 2026).
OCP Group's 2025 revenue rose 17.5% to MAD 113.9 billion (about US$11.4 billion); net income fell 13% on higher taxes.
Tanger Med handled 11.1 million TEU in 2025, up 8.4%. Works on the Dakhla Atlantique port passed 74% at end-September 2026, with completion planned for end-2028.

ECOWAS leaders signed the Nigeria–Morocco gas pipeline agreement on July 19, 2026: up to 30 bcm a year, cost estimates of $25–27 billion, first gas targeted for 2031. No final investment decision yet.
